title: Universal first order thickening of a scheme over another
statement: Let $h:Z\to X$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. A *universal first order thickening of $Z$ over $X$* is a first order thickening $Z\subset Z'$ over $X$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], that is a scheme $Z'$ with a morphism $h':Z'\to X$ and a closed immersion $i_Z:Z\to Z'$ whose ideal sheaf has square zero, with $h'\circ i_Z=h$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base], such that the following holds: for every first order thickening $T\subset T'$ over $X$ (closed immersion $i_T:T\to T'$, structure morphism $b:T'\to X$; $T$ and $T'$ arbitrary schemes, not necessarily affine) and every morphism $a:T\to Z$ with $h\circ a=b\circ i_T$, there is exactly one morphism $a':T'\to Z'$ with $h'\circ a'=b$ and $a'\circ i_T=i_Z\circ a$.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Section 04F2 (section-universal-thickening), opening paragraph; Definition 04F4 (definition-universal-thickening) (1)
